key_insight: Changing the interpolation path in flow matching can greatly reduce stochastic-gradient variance and speed up SGD, even when the underlying FM objective is identical.
engineering_relevance: Path choice is a practical optimization knob for training faster, more stable generative models without changing the target distribution.
method: Analyze SGD variance for different paths inducing the same marginals/velocity field.
Derive a tight iteration-complexity bound and optimal linear path in a 1D Gaussian setting.
Formulate a sample-estimable PathOpt problem to search for low-variance paths under the FM equivalence constraint.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the theory with experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets.
watch_item: Variance reduction must respect the constraint that paths stay in the same FM equivalence class; otherwise lower variance can paradoxically slow convergence.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
